title: What is associated with race performance in male 100-km ultra-marathoners - anthropometry, training or marathon best time?
authors: Knechtle B, Knechtle P, Rosemann T, Senn O
population: 93 recreational male 100-km ultra-marathoners (mean age 44.6 years, BMI 23.4)
findings: Bivariate correlations with 100-km race time: personal best marathon time r = 0.72, percent body fat r = 0.57, sum of eight skinfolds r = 0.55, weekly running km r = -0.49, training running speed r = -0.50, weekly running hours r = -0.29, BMI r = 0.24.
Multiple regression: weekly running kilometres and average training speed were independently and negatively associated with race time; the sum of skinfolds was positively associated.
Training and anthropometry remained relevant when controlling for marathon personal best.
limitations: Small, male-only, road 100 km, cross-sectional; no coefficients or prediction error in the abstract; no trail or elevation.
implications: Use marathon personal best as the primary anchor for road ultra predictions (r = 0.72), then adjust for weekly kilometres and habitual training pace.
No numeric coefficients can be taken from the abstract; do not hard-code a formula.

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC re-fetched; all correlations match.
